questions.text: The highest mountain peak of Pakistan is
questions.explanation: K2, at 8,611 metres, is the highest peak in Pakistan and the second highest in the world after Mount Everest.

questions.text: K2 is situated in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: K2 stands in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan-China frontier in Gilgit-Baltistan.

questions.text: Nanga Parbat lies in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: Nanga Parbat, 8,126 metres high, is the western anchor of the Himalayan range and lies in Diamer district.

questions.text: The highest peak of the Hindu Kush range is
questions.explanation: Tirich Mir, 7,708 metres, in Chitral district is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush.

questions.text: How many peaks above 8,000 metres are located in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Pakistan has five eight-thousanders: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak and Gasherbrum II.

questions.text: The Siachen Glacier lies in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: Siachen is a long glacier of the eastern Karakoram range and is the world's highest battleground.

questions.text: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with
questions.explanation: The Khunjerab Pass in Gilgit-Baltistan is the border crossing between Pakistan and China's Xinjiang region.

questions.text: The Khyber Pass links Pakistan with
questions.explanation: The Khyber Pass runs from Peshawar valley through the Safed Koh to Afghanistan and has been the historic invasion route into the subcontinent.

questions.text: The Shandur Pass connects Chitral with
questions.explanation: Shandur, the site of the world's highest polo ground, links Chitral with Gilgit.

questions.text: The Lowari Pass provides a route between Chitral and
questions.explanation: The Lowari Pass, now bypassed by the Lowari Tunnel, connects Chitral with the Dir district.

questions.text: The Babusar Pass links the Kaghan Valley with
questions.explanation: Babusar Top joins the upper Kaghan Valley to Chilas on the Karakoram Highway.

questions.text: The Indus River rises in
questions.explanation: The Indus originates in the Tibetan plateau near Lake Mansarovar before entering Gilgit-Baltistan.

questions.text: The Kabul River joins the Indus at
questions.explanation: The Kabul River meets the Indus near Attock, just below Khairabad.

questions.text: The Panjnad River joins the Indus near
questions.explanation: The combined waters of the five eastern rivers form the Panjnad, which enters the Indus at Mithankot.

questions.text: Tarbela Dam is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Tarbela, in Swabi district, is an earth-filled dam on the Indus completed in 1976.

questions.text: Mangla Dam is constructed on which river?
questions.explanation: Mangla Dam, completed in 1967, impounds the Jhelum River near Mirpur in Azad Kashmir.

questions.text: Warsak Dam has been built on which river?
questions.explanation: Warsak Dam lies on the Kabul River about twenty kilometres from Peshawar.

questions.text: The Diamer-Bhasha Dam is being constructed on which river?
questions.explanation: Diamer-Bhasha is a concrete gravity dam on the Indus upstream of Tarbela.

questions.text: The Mohmand Dam is being built on which river?
questions.explanation: Mohmand Dam is a hydropower and storage project on the Swat River in Mohmand district.

questions.text: The Sukkur Barrage on the Indus was completed in
questions.explanation: Formerly called the Lloyd Barrage, Sukkur Barrage was completed in 1932 and feeds one of the world's largest irrigation systems.

questions.text: The Ghulam Muhammad Barrage on the Indus is commonly known as
questions.explanation: Kotri Barrage near Hyderabad is officially named the Ghulam Muhammad Barrage and is the lowest barrage on the Indus.

questions.text: The largest desert of Pakistan is the
questions.explanation: The Thar Desert of southeastern Sindh is the largest desert in Pakistan and extends into Indian Rajasthan.

questions.text: The Thal Desert lies between the Indus and which other river?
questions.explanation: Thal occupies the doab between the Indus and the Jhelum in districts such as Bhakkar and Layyah.

questions.text: The largest freshwater lake of Pakistan is
questions.explanation: Manchar Lake in Sindh, west of the Indus, is the largest natural freshwater lake in Pakistan.

questions.text: Keenjhar Lake mainly supplies drinking water to which city?
questions.explanation: Keenjhar (Kalri) Lake in Thatta district is the principal source of piped water for Karachi.

questions.text: Lake Saiful Muluk is located in which valley?
questions.explanation: Saiful Muluk is an alpine lake near Naran in the Kaghan Valley of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

questions.text: Attabad Lake, formed by a landslide in 2010, lies in which valley?
questions.explanation: A massive landslide at Attabad in January 2010 blocked the Hunza River and created the lake.

questions.text: Hanna Lake is situated near which city?
questions.explanation: Hanna Lake lies in the Urak valley a short distance from Quetta.

questions.text: The largest province of Pakistan by area is
questions.explanation: Balochistan covers about 347,190 square kilometres, roughly 44 per cent of Pakistan's territory.

questions.text: The total area of Pakistan is approximately
questions.explanation: Pakistan's area is officially given as 796,096 square kilometres.

questions.text: The length of Pakistan's coastline is approximately
questions.explanation: Pakistan's Arabian Sea coastline of about 1,046 kilometres is shared between Sindh and Balochistan.

questions.text: Pakistan's shortest international land border is with
questions.explanation: The Pakistan-China boundary along the Karakoram is the shortest of Pakistan's land borders.

questions.text: The Durand Line between Pakistan and Afghanistan was demarcated in
questions.explanation: The line was agreed in 1893 between Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan of Afghanistan.

questions.text: The Sir Creek dispute concerns the boundary between Sindh and the Indian state of
questions.explanation: Sir Creek is a tidal estuary in the Rann of Kutch marking the disputed Sindh-Gujarat maritime boundary.

questions.text: Gwadar was purchased by Pakistan in 1958 from
questions.explanation: Gwadar had been an enclave of the Sultanate of Oman and was bought by Pakistan in 1958.

questions.text: Port Qasim is located near which city?
questions.explanation: Port Qasim, Pakistan's second busiest port, lies on the Indus delta creeks southeast of Karachi.

questions.text: The Khewra Salt Mine is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Khewra, in Jhelum district of Punjab, is one of the largest rock-salt mines in the world.

questions.text: The Saindak copper and gold project is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Saindak lies in Chagai district of Balochistan near the Iranian and Afghan borders.

questions.text: The Sui gas field lies in which district of Balochistan?
questions.explanation: Sui is located in Dera Bugti district in eastern Balochistan.

questions.text: The Mari gas field is located in which province?
questions.explanation: The Mari gas field lies near Daharki in the Ghotki area of upper Sindh.

questions.text: The Thar coalfield is located in which province?
questions.explanation: The Thar lignite deposits in Tharparkar district of Sindh are among the largest coal reserves in the world.

questions.text: Muslim Bagh, known for chromite mining, is located in which province?
questions.explanation: Muslim Bagh in Killa Saifullah district of Balochistan is Pakistan's main chromite producing area.

questions.text: Emerald mines in Pakistan are chiefly located in which valley?
questions.explanation: The emerald deposits near Mingora in the Swat valley are Pakistan's best known source of the gemstone.

questions.text: Kalabagh, known for its iron ore deposits, lies in which district?
questions.explanation: The Kalabagh iron ore field is in Mianwali district of Punjab on the right bank of the Indus.

questions.text: The Deosai Plains are located in
questions.explanation: Deosai, near Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan, is one of the highest plateaus in the world and a national park.

questions.text: The Salt Range lies between the Jhelum River and which other river?
questions.explanation: The Salt Range stretches across northern Punjab between the Jhelum and the Indus, south of the Potohar Plateau.

questions.text: The largest national park of Pakistan by area is
questions.explanation: Hingol National Park on the Makran coast of Balochistan is the largest national park in Pakistan.

questions.text: Astola Island, the largest island of Pakistan, lies off the coast of
questions.explanation: Astola, also called Jezira Haft Talar, lies in the Arabian Sea off the Makran coast near Pasni.

questions.text: The capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir is
questions.explanation: Muzaffarabad, on the confluence of the Neelum and Jhelum rivers, is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.text: Changa Manga, one of the largest planted forests of Pakistan, is located in which province?
questions.explanation: Changa Manga is a man-made irrigated plantation in Kasur district of Punjab.

questions.text: The monsoon rains in Pakistan generally occur between
questions.explanation: The summer monsoon reaches Pakistan in early July and withdraws by September, bringing most of the annual rainfall.

questions.text: The largest food crop of Pakistan in terms of area sown is
questions.explanation: Wheat, a Rabi crop, occupies the largest cultivated area and is the staple food grain of Pakistan.

questions.text: The province producing the largest share of Pakistan's cotton is
questions.explanation: Punjab's southern districts account for the greater part of national cotton output, with Sindh second.

questions.text: Faisalabad is popularly known as
questions.explanation: Faisalabad earned the title because of its concentration of cotton textile mills.

questions.text: Sialkot is chiefly known for the manufacture of
questions.explanation: Sialkot is the centre of Pakistan's sports goods, leather and surgical instrument industries.

questions.text: Pakistan Steel Mills was set up with the technical and financial assistance of
questions.explanation: The Karachi steel mill was built at Pipri under a 1971 agreement with the Soviet Union.

questions.text: The Heavy Mechanical Complex of Pakistan is located at
questions.explanation: The Heavy Mechanical Complex at Taxila, built with Chinese assistance, manufactures industrial plant and machinery.

questions.text: Pakistan's first nuclear power plant, KANUPP, began operating in
questions.explanation: The Karachi Nuclear Power Plant, built with Canadian assistance, was commissioned in 1972.

questions.text: The State Bank of Pakistan was established on
questions.explanation: The State Bank of Pakistan was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah on 1 July 1948.

questions.text: The fiscal year of the Government of Pakistan runs from
questions.explanation: Pakistan's financial year begins on 1 July and closes on 30 June.

questions.text: The largest single category of Pakistan's exports is
questions.explanation: Textiles and made-up garments have long accounted for roughly three-fifths of Pakistan's export earnings.

questions.text: The largest group of Pakistan's imports by value is
questions.explanation: Petroleum crude and refined products form Pakistan's biggest import bill and drive its trade deficit.

questions.text: The Economic Survey of Pakistan is published each year by the
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Finance issues the Economic Survey a day before the federal budget is presented.

questions.text: The Pakistan Stock Exchange was created in 2016 by merging the stock exchanges of
questions.explanation: The Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad stock exchanges were integrated into the Pakistan Stock Exchange in January 2016.

questions.text: The nationalization of major industries, banks and insurance companies in Pakistan was carried out under
questions.explanation: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's government began nationalizing basic industries in 1972 and banks in 1974.

questions.text: The Green Revolution in Pakistan's agriculture took place mainly during the government of
questions.explanation: High-yielding seed varieties, tubewells and fertilizer use spread rapidly in the 1960s under Ayub Khan.

questions.text: Pakistan's First Five Year Plan covered the period
questions.explanation: The First Five Year Plan ran from 1955 to 1960, though it was formally approved only in 1957.

questions.text: The Motorway M-2 connects Islamabad with
questions.explanation: The M-2, Pakistan's first motorway, links Islamabad with Lahore and was opened in 1997.

questions.text: National Highway N-5, the Grand Trunk Road, runs from Karachi to
questions.explanation: N-5 is Pakistan's longest national highway, running from Karachi through Lahore and Rawalpindi to Peshawar.

questions.text: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor links Gwadar with which Chinese city?
questions.explanation: CPEC connects Gwadar port to Kashgar in China's Xinjiang region by road, rail and pipeline routes.

questions.text: The main CPEC agreements were signed in April 2015 during the visit to Pakistan of
questions.explanation: Chinese President Xi Jinping's April 2015 visit produced the package of CPEC agreements worth about 46 billion dollars.

questions.text: The operational control of Gwadar Port was transferred in 2013 to a company of
questions.explanation: Operations passed from the Port of Singapore Authority to the China Overseas Ports Holding Company in 2013.

questions.text: The Indus Waters Treaty between Pakistan and India was signed in
questions.explanation: The treaty was signed on 19 September 1960 after nine years of negotiation.

questions.text: The Indus Waters Treaty was negotiated through the good offices of
questions.explanation: The World Bank mediated the dispute and remains a signatory and guarantor of the treaty.

questions.text: Under the Indus Waters Treaty the eastern rivers allotted to India are
questions.explanation: India received unrestricted use of the Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, while Pakistan received the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab.

questions.text: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed on behalf of Pakistan by
questions.explanation: President Ayub Khan signed for Pakistan and Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru for India.

questions.text: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in which city?
questions.explanation: The treaty was signed at Karachi, then the capital of Pakistan, in September 1960.

questions.text: The body established under the Indus Waters Treaty to handle routine questions between the two countries is the
questions.explanation: Each country appoints an Indus Commissioner, and together they form the Permanent Indus Commission.

questions.text: The ceasefire ending the first Kashmir war between Pakistan and India came into effect on
questions.explanation: A United Nations sponsored ceasefire took effect on 1 January 1949 and produced the ceasefire line in Kashmir.

questions.text: The 1965 war between Pakistan and India on the international border began on
questions.explanation: Indian forces crossed the international border towards Lahore on 6 September 1965, now observed as Defence Day.

questions.text: The Pakistani operation launched in Kashmir in August 1965 was code-named
questions.explanation: Operation Gibraltar sent infiltrators into Indian-held Kashmir and led to the escalation of the 1965 war.

questions.text: The Tashkent Declaration ending the 1965 war was signed in
questions.explanation: Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri signed the declaration on 10 January 1966.

questions.text: The Tashkent talks of 1966 were mediated by
questions.explanation: Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin hosted and mediated the talks at Tashkent in Soviet Uzbekistan.

questions.text: Dhaka fell to Indian forces on
questions.explanation: The Pakistani eastern command surrendered at Dhaka on 16 December 1971, ending the war in East Pakistan.

questions.text: The Simla Agreement was signed by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and
questions.explanation: Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi signed the agreement with Pakistan's President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

questions.text: Pakistan formally recognized Bangladesh in
questions.explanation: Pakistan recognized Bangladesh in February 1974, shortly before the second Islamic Summit at Lahore.

questions.text: The second Islamic Summit Conference was held in 1974 at
questions.explanation: Lahore hosted the second summit of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference in February 1974.

questions.text: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests of 28 May 1998 in the hills of
questions.explanation: Five devices were detonated in the Ras Koh Hills of Chagai district on 28 May 1998.

questions.text: The first Prime Minister of Pakistan was assassinated in 1951 at
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan was shot on 16 October 1951 at Company Bagh, Rawalpindi, later renamed Liaquat Bagh.

questions.text: The first Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan in October 1958 was
questions.explanation: When martial law was proclaimed on 7 October 1958, General Ayub Khan was appointed Chief Martial Law Administrator.

questions.text: General Zia-ul-Haq imposed martial law in Pakistan on
questions.explanation: Zia-ul-Haq removed the Bhutto government in Operation Fair Play on 5 July 1977.

questions.text: General Zia-ul-Haq died in an air crash in 1988 near
questions.explanation: The presidential aircraft crashed shortly after take-off from Bahawalpur on 17 August 1988.

questions.text: The first woman to become Prime Minister of Pakistan was
questions.explanation: Benazir Bhutto took office in December 1988 as the first woman prime minister of Pakistan.

questions.text: The first general elections in Pakistan held on the basis of adult franchise took place in
questions.explanation: The December 1970 polls were Pakistan's first direct general elections on universal adult franchise.

questions.text: Which city served as the interim capital of Pakistan while Islamabad was under construction?
questions.explanation: Rawalpindi functioned as the interim capital from 1959 until Islamabad was ready to receive the government.

questions.text: Pakistan became a member of the United Nations on
questions.explanation: Pakistan was admitted to the United Nations on 30 September 1947, six weeks after independence.

questions.text: The highest civil award of Pakistan is
questions.explanation: Nishan-e-Pakistan is the highest civil decoration, usually conferred on foreign heads of state and government.

questions.text: The first recipient of Nishan-e-Haider was
questions.explanation: Captain Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed was awarded the first Nishan-e-Haider for gallantry in Kashmir in 1948.

questions.text: The only officer of the Pakistan Air Force awarded the Nishan-e-Haider is
questions.explanation: Pilot Officer Rashid Minhas received the award for preventing the hijacking of his aircraft to India in 1971.

questions.text: Captain Karnal Sher Khan was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider for gallantry in
questions.explanation: Captain Karnal Sher Khan received the award posthumously for his defence of positions in the Kargil sector in 1999.

questions.text: The national flower of Pakistan is
questions.explanation: Jasmine, known locally as chambeli, is the national flower of Pakistan.

questions.text: The national tree of Pakistan is
questions.explanation: The Himalayan cedar or deodar is the national tree of Pakistan.

questions.text: The national animal of Pakistan is the
questions.explanation: The markhor, a wild goat of the northern mountains, is Pakistan's national animal.

questions.text: The national bird of Pakistan is the
questions.explanation: The chukar partridge is recognized as the national bird of Pakistan.

questions.text: The national sport of Pakistan is
questions.explanation: Field hockey is Pakistan's national game, in which the country has won several Olympic and World Cup titles.

questions.text: The words of Pakistan's national anthem were written by
questions.explanation: Abu-al-Asar Hafeez Jalandhari wrote the lyrics of the Qaumi Taranah.

questions.text: The music of Pakistan's national anthem was composed by
questions.explanation: Ahmed Ghulamali Chagla composed the tune, which was approved before the lyrics were selected.

questions.text: The national anthem of Pakistan was officially adopted in
questions.explanation: The Qaumi Taranah was formally adopted in August 1954 and first broadcast on Radio Pakistan.

questions.text: The national flag of Pakistan was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly approved the design of the national flag on 11 August 1947.

questions.text: The white stripe in the national flag of Pakistan represents
questions.explanation: The vertical white band stands for the non-Muslim minorities of Pakistan, while the green field represents the Muslim majority.
